rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful performance baseline. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only, single-profile, PCA representation without aggregation or fusion, giving a low-confound reference for validation accuracy and F1. This is the best first use of budget because it calibrates the search before testing multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only, or multimodal fusion.

The only completed result is config_001, an RNA-only single-profile PCA model with validation accuracy 0.4849 and F1 0.4639, leaving uncertainty about whether multiple RNA profiles with simple aggregation improve over the single-profile baseline. config_002 keeps the model setting and RNA encoder fixed while testing multiprofile with avgpool, directly isolating the effect of profile setting/aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal, interpretable extension of the existing baseline, reduces uncertainty before adding image modality or more complex encoders, and creates a multiprofile RNA reference for later multimodal comparisons.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool improves validation accuracy and F1 over singleprofile RNA, but it is unclear whether a more expressive transformer aggregation further helps. config_003 tests only the aggregation factor while keeping the same RNA encoder and profile setting, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it minimally extends the currently best configuration and reduces uncertainty about aggregation before adding new encoders or modalities.

config_002 shows that multiprofile avgpool PCA RNA is currently the strongest setting, with both higher accuracy and F1 than singleprofile or transformer, so profile/aggregation is a promising direction. The major remaining uncertainty is whether image data contains useful signal and whether the same multiprofile avgpool setting transfers to image. config_011 tests an image-only ResNet50 model under that same profile/aggregation, isolating modality/representation before introducing fusion. This is a simpler, high-information experiment: if image is competitive, multimodal fusion becomes well motivated; if not, we avoid confounding image, fusion, and model setting in one multimodal run.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the strongest completed result (0.591 acc, 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet multiprofile avgpool is weak (0.328 acc, 0.288 F1). The key uncertainty is whether the image modality adds complementary signal under the best profile/aggregation setting. config_018 tests the simplest multimodal extension by adding concat fusion with the same PCA RNA, ResNet image, multiprofile, and avgpool settings, isolating the effect of fusion without changing representation, profile, or aggregation. This is the best next budget use because it exploits the strongest RNA baseline and determines whether further investment in image/fusion is justified before testing more complex encoders or fusion variants.

Completed runs show RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is strong (0.591 acc / 0.573 F1) and the only multimodal run, config_018 with concat fusion, is best (0.619 acc / 0.610 F1) but only slightly better and only one fusion method has been tested. config_019 keeps the same model, profile, encoders, and aggregation but changes fusion to weighted, isolating the fusion effect. This is a minimal one-factor extension of the current best, so it can confirm whether the multimodal advantage is robust and whether fusion tuning can improve performance before spending budget on larger changes such as new image or RNA encoders.

The strongest evidence so far is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile PCA/ResNet weighted-fusion model with avgpool aggregation, achieving the best validation accuracy and F1. RNA-only results suggest multiprofile avgpool can help, but it is still unclear whether multiprofile aggregation is actually needed in the multimodal setting or whether the gain comes mainly from adding image features. Config_017 tests the same multimodal weighted PCA/ResNet setup with singleprofile, directly clarifying whether the multiprofile/aggregation component is driving the improvement or whether a simpler singleprofile model is sufficient. This is the best next experiment because it is a clean comparison within the currently strongest family, avoids assuming that multiprofile complexity is necessary, and will guide whether to keep or simplify the architecture before exploring new encoders or aggregators.

The strongest completed setup is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted) with validation accuracy 0.639 and F1 0.620, indicating that multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion are useful, and that image features add modest value over RNA-only. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising direction is image representation: only ResNet50 has been tested, and image-only ResNet50 performed weakly, so it is unclear whether a stronger ViT encoder can improve the multimodal model. config_025 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the best-known profile, RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed, so it cleanly isolates the effect of image representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best configuration while efficiently reducing uncertainty about a high-impact design choice.

The strongest result so far is config_019, a multimodal multiprofile model with pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion, achieving 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1. RNA-only evidence suggests avgpool aggregation is better than transformer aggregation, but it is unclear whether that holds when image features are included. config_021 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the otherwise best multimodal setup, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve performance or whether avgpool is robust in the multimodal setting. This is a clean, single-factor comparison in the most promising region, making it an efficient use of the next experiment.

The strongest completed experiment is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted, resnet50, PCA) with validation accuracy 0.639 and F1 0.620. Matched comparisons suggest weighted fusion is better than concat and avgpool is better than transformer, while the main untested important factor in this best branch is RNA representation, since only PCA has been tested so far. config_031 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping the best-known profile setting, aggregation, fusion, and image encoder fixed, so it directly tests whether a learned RNA representation improves over PCA. This is a focused exploitation of the current best direction and efficiently reduces uncertainty about a major design choice under a limited budget.
